title: Synchronous RPC within Database Transactions
pattern: Executing a remote RPC call, HTTP request, or socket write inside an active database transaction block (e.g., between `BEGIN TRANSACTION` and `COMMIT`), especially when holding pessimistic row locks (e.g., `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`).
why_bad: A database transaction is designed to be short-lived, with memory and disk footprint tracking managed locally [6]. Remote RPC latency is highly variable and can take seconds due to timeouts or packet drops [113]. Holding exclusive database locks open while waiting for external network IO severely spikes transaction duration, starves other database threads, exhausts database connection pools, and can freeze the entire application [6, 7].
detection: Identify blocks representing active transactions (e.g., closure arguments in transaction execution or code blocks between a database connection's `.transaction()` and `.commit()`) that invoke functions belonging to remote clients or HTTP wrappers.
fix: Refactor the logic to perform all external network communication outside of the database transaction boundary. Ensure transactions only execute quick, local read and write operations.
